title: Spinach Soup
subtitle: Silky blended spinach soup with nutmeg and cream
excerpt: A bright green, silky soup made from wilted spinach blended with stock, onion, and a little double cream. Ready in under 20 minutes. Finish with a grating of nutmeg.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spinach soup has been made in British kitchens since spinach was introduced from Persia via Spain in the 16th century. The soup is notable for its speed: spinach wilts in seconds and the entire dish takes under 20 minutes from start to finish. The colour fades from bright green to khaki if left on heat too long after blending: serve immediately once blended, or plunge the base into an ice bath to preserve the colour if making ahead.

recipeTools.notes: Plus a blender or stick blender.

content.text: The colour is the most perishable thing about this soup: blend immediately and serve straight away. If making ahead, cool the base rapidly and blend only when reheating. Do not let the soup boil after adding the cream.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock. Bring to a boil. Add all the spinach and push it under the liquid. Cook for 2 minutes until completely wilted.
Remove from the heat. Blend until completely smooth with a stick blender or in a jug blender. Stir in the cream and nutmeg. Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.
